title.narrative: Output 1.3. Increased institutional capacity of labour administrations

description.narrative:
The current Memorandum of Understanding 2020-22 (MoU) between the Royal Government of Cambodia (RGC), Garment Manufacturers Association in Cambodia (GMAC) and the ILO expanded the scope of RGC's mandatory working condition assessments conducted annually in every garment sector factory by Better Factories Cambodia (BFC) programme to an additional sector, travel goods and bag sector (covering currently around 90 factories). A plan towards improved compliance on core labour standards and the labour law in this sector has been initiated through RGC's regulation stating the mandatory and complementary monitoring by BFC (in order for factories to obtain their export license).
MOLVT and its labour inspectorate has started collaborating with BFC on capacity building for improved compliance and assessment methodologies of its labour inspectors for conducting joint assessments for factories in this sector – outlined in the Joint Action Plan between BFC and MOLVT 2020-22. Better Factories Cambodia (BFC) has supported the plan to combine efforts between Ministry of Labour and Vocational Training (MoLVT) inspection and BFC towards joint assessment in travel goods factories – trainings on child labour prevention, industrial relations and OSH have been conducted virtually, in 2021 in collaboration with MOLVT and Garment Manufacturers Association (GMAC), to the majority (around 60) of the registered exporting travel goods and bag factories in Cambodia.

description.narrative: The tripartite Labour Advisory Committee of Cambodia, and Ministry of Labour and Vocational Training (MoLVT) adopted in May 2021 the COVID-19 related OSH and working condition instructions and guidance that were based on recommendations from WHO and Better Factories Cambodia (BFC). The COVID-19 instructions targeted the reopening of the several hundred garment factories affected by the lockdown in April and May, following an increase of positive cases also in the factories. Better Factories Cambodia (BFC) and World Health Organization (WHO)/Center for Disease Control (CDC) jointly supported the Royal Government of Cambodia in developing a joint risk assessment for factories, risk based preventative/mitigation recommendations for factories, factory assessment checklist, and the development of a contact tracing Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) for opening the factories after the lockdown in 2021 – the Ministry of Labour and Vocational Training (MoLVT) instruction to factories in May 2021 was based on these recommendations. At least 300 persons participated to a joint training webinar.
